# @openphenology/api

> TypeScript client for OpenPhenology's published data: when each species is recorded, week by week, in US counties and states. ESM only, no dependencies, Node.js 22+ and current browsers. Read-only; no keys or accounts. Data is published in dated releases that never change.

Beta: OpenPhenology and this package are in beta; the interface may change before 1.0.0, while published file formats change only by version.

Not live yet: until the first data release is published, `client.release()` rejects with `ApiError` code `not-found`, because `current.json` does not exist yet.

## Start

```js
import { createClient } from "@openphenology/api";

const release = await createClient().release(); // current release, read once
const key = await release.speciesBySlug("northern-cardinal"); // string | null
if (key) {
  const result = await release.countyResult("us-oh", "39049", key); // null if none
  console.log(result?.data.season); // [early, middle, late] weeks, or []
}
```

## Codes every read takes

- State: `us-` + postal abbreviation, e.g. `us-oh`.
- County: 5-digit Census code (GEOID), e.g. `39049`. List a state's counties with `release.region("us-oh")`; from a ZIP code use `release.zipCounties("43215")`, which returns `{ area, state, share }[]`, largest share first. `countyState("39049")` gives a county's state code (`us-oh`).
- Species key: from `release.speciesBySlug(slug)`, `release.searchNames()` (`[name, kind, key]` triples) or `release.catalogue()`.
- Release ID: its date, e.g. `2026-10-19`.

A malformed code is a `RangeError` before any request is made.

## Client

- `createClient(options?)` → `Client`. Options: `baseUrl`, `release` (pin an ID), `verify` (check SHA-256 against the manifest), `timeoutMs` (default 10000), `retries` (default 2; after network errors, 429 and 5xx), `signal`, `fetch`.
- `client.release({ refresh? })` → `Release`. Without `refresh`, the same release every call. `refresh: true` re-reads `current.json`; existing `Release` objects keep their own files.
- `client.current()` → `current.json`: the current release and when it was published. `client.releases()` → every release and its status. `client.terms()` → licence (CC BY-NC 4.0, noncommercial use), how to cite and credit.

## Release (each returns the parsed file, or `null` when not published; lists are empty instead)

- Species: `catalogue()` → `CatalogueEntry[]`; `species(key)`; `speciesBySlug(slug)` → key or `null`; `groups()`; `searchNames()` → `SearchName[]`.
- Places: `region(state)`; `boundaries(state)` (GeoJSON county outlines, display only); `zipCounties(zip)` → `ZipCounty[]`; `postal(prefix)` (every ZIP code with a 3-digit prefix, for suggestions).
- Results: `stateResult(state, species)`; `countyResult(state, county, species)`; `backyard(state, county)`; `attribution(state, species, county?)`.
- The release: `manifest()`; `notes()`; `methods()`; `sources()`.

Every file is `{ id, kind, format, provenance, data }`; read `file.data`.

## Reading results

- Results show when people recorded a species, not when or where it occurs. Low or zero counts do not mean absence.
- Weeks 1–53: week 1 is 1–7 January, week 53 the last one or two days. Every weekly list has 53 values. `weekOf(date)` gives a date's week (UTC); `WEEKS` is 53. These helpers, `countyState`, `PRODUCTION_URL` and `STAGING_URL` also come from `@openphenology/api/format`, which does not load the reader.
- `data.weekly.records`: the species' records per week. `data.weekly.years`: years contributing per week. `data.effort`: records of all species in the same place and week.
- `data.season`: `[early, middle, late]` weeks (5th, 50th, 95th percentiles), or `[]` with `data.season_withheld` set to `year-round`, `two-seasons`, `one-year` or `precision`.
- Backyard `labels`: a 53-letter string, one per week: `c` commonly reported, `s` seasonally reported, `r` reported in your area, `m` within its mapped range, `n` not enough evidence. `backyardLabel(labels, week)` reads one week's letter; `BACKYARD_LABELS[letter]` names it.
- A withheld result (sensitive species, or too little evidence) is not published, so it reads as `null`, the same as no result.
- Species `data.statuses` (from `species/1.1`): the species' listings on the federal Endangered Species Act list and Ohio's lists, each with `list`, `place`, `listed_name`, `status` and `where`. Only government lists are published.
- Species `data.introductions` (from `species/1.2`): the species' US-RIIS listings in the lower 48 states, each with `source`, `region`, `listed_name` and `status` (`introduced` or `invasive`). An empty list never means native.
- Species area `conditions` (from `species/1.7`): medians over the result's records of `sunrise` and `sunset` (local `HH:MM`) and the daily `high`, `low` and `midpoint` (°C, NOAA nClimGrid-Daily, lower 48 states only). `midpoint` is the mean of the day's high and low. A value is `null` when too few records have it. They describe the days the records were made, not why or what a species needs.
- Species area `flowering` (from `species/1.8`): for a plant, the result from its records that show flowers, with `records`, `season` and `season_withheld` (which may be `too-few-records`); `null` for a species that is not a plant. It describes when people recorded the plant with flowers showing, not when it flowers: say "reported in flower" and name the middle week, never a peak.
- Species area `windows` (from `species/1.9`): when `season_withheld` is `two-seasons`, the two windows the records split into, each with `records`, `season` and `season_withheld` (which may be `too-few-records`); otherwise `null`. A flowering result has `windows` the same way. Say when the species was recorded in each window, never why there are two.
- Species area `record_dates` and `latest_month` (from `species/1.10`): how many distinct dates the result's counted records fall on, and the month (`YYYY-MM`) of the latest of them. Both are `null` for a species sensitive in the state. They say when people recorded the species, never whether it is there now.
- Species `data.inaturalist_taxon_id` (from `species/1.3`): the iNaturalist taxon ID, or `null`.
- Search name kinds: `scientific`, `common`, `other-name` (other English common names, from `search/1.1`) and `synonym`.
- Backyard species (from `backyard/1.1`): `records`, `weekly` (53 values), `season` and `season_withheld` repeat the county result; `null`, `null`, `[]` and `null` without one.
- Manifest (`manifest/2.0`): `data.parts` is how many parts it has. A large manifest is split on `files`: `manifest.json`, then `manifest/1.json` and so on. `manifest()` joins them, so `data.files` is always complete. `manifest/1.0` has no `parts` and is still read.
- `archive.tar.gz`: every file of a release except the manifest's parts, in one download. The manifest lists it with `format` `null`; check it against its `sha256`.

## Errors

Branch on `error.code`; messages may change.

- `ApiError` (has `url`, `status`): `network`, `timeout`, `aborted`, `status`, `not-found`, `release-unavailable`.
- `FormatError` (has `path`): `not-json`, `wrong-kind`, `unsupported-version`, `malformed`, `checksum`.
- `RangeError`: a malformed code.

## Files in this package

- `dist/index.d.ts`: every type and method, with doc comments.
- `schemas/<kind>-<major>.json`: JSON Schema 2020-12 for each format, every field described. The major is 1, except `manifest-2.json`.
- `schemas/all-1.json`: every schema in one file, by kind.
- `schemas/examples/<kind>-<major>.json`: one made-up example file per format.
- Kinds: current, releases, terms, manifest, notes, catalogue, species, slugs, groups, search, region, state-weekly, county-weekly, attribution, backyard, methods, sources, boundaries, postal.
- `README.md`: the same, with more examples.

Outside the package, the repository's `postman/openphenology.postman_collection.json` is a Postman collection with one request per file kind, with descriptions, examples and schema tests; `postman/README.md` explains it.
